messages:
alex: Heads up — noticed a perf regression after the runtime KV paging change. Mixtral MQA workloads are fragmented and throughput dropped. attaching quick profile

sara: link? what scope is this (prod/dedicated/canary)?

alex: canary. Mixtral-8x MQA and Qwen-7B GQA behave differently. Mixtral MQA sees ~-22% throughput under heavy prefix load (>8k active seqs). profile snapshot shows a lot of memcpy and kernel striding overhead.

jamal: what are the current kv-layout/config values? num_key_value_heads? kv_dim? page size?

alex: current runtime defaults: num_key_value_heads: 32, kv_dim: 1280, kv_page_size: 4096. RoPE scaling tweak landed last week (see loader change) which also adjusted per-layer stride calc.

maria: that mismatch (heads vs physical layout) will cause non-coalesced loads on the attention kernel. If num_kv_heads doesn't align with warp-friendly groupings we pay mem bandwidth.

alex: perf top snippet: 
```
memcpy: 34%
kernel-launch overhead: 18%
attention_per_head_stride: 26%
other (CPU prep, locking): 22%
```

sara: I ran a microbench on the canary. switching KV layout from "interleaved-per-head" -> "contiguous-per-layer" drops memcpy to ~12% and improves kernel utilization.

jamal: did you also try changing page size? tiny pages + many fragments = extra GPU-side bookkeeping. 4KB pages for large kv_dim result in many pages per token slot.

alex: tried bumping kv_page_size to 65536 in a local build: fragmentation reduced, number of page lookups down 3x. tradeoffs: memory usage + about 7%. perf: throughput +11%, p99 down ~19%.

maria: RoPE note: the recent RoPE scaling change made us recompute scale tables per-layer at every callsite; that's adding CPU time and increased kernel launch churn. Cache the table per-device and reuse across batches. small win but noticeable for short batches.

jamal: kernel selector idea: if num_kv_heads % 8 != 0 or kv_dim % 64 != 0 prefer the head-split (strided) kernel that uses per-head packing. else prefer contiguous fused kernel (flash-attn path). Also pick fused path when seq_len>1024 and batch_size>8.

alex: config snippet I tested: 
```
{
  "num_key_value_heads": 16,
  "kv_dim": 640,
  "kv_page_size": 65536,
  "kv_layout": "contiguous_per_layer"
}
```

sara: microbench numbers (Mixtral MQA): baseline 8800 tok/s -> after contiguous layout + 64KB pages -> 9800 tok/s (+11.3%). p99 latency 210ms -> 170ms. CPU worker threads also drop context-switches.

jamal: good. we should add a runtime heuristic: for MQA models with kv_dim>512 choose 64KB pages; for small models use 16KB default. And a kernel selector based on head alignment.

maria: found one more regression in dedicated: the kv cache eviction loop was using a global mutex; moving to per-shard locks increased concurrency and removed a contention hotspot.

ops-bot: deploy: canary upgraded to 4 nodes with patched runtime (kv-layout + 64KB pages + kernel-selector). perf-check jobs queued.

alex: I'll open a PR with the kernel selector, page-size heuristic, and a small RoPE caching patch. Need reviewers for eng-runtime and eng-ml model loader side. I'll include perf tests for Mixtral, Llama-2, and Qwen.

sara: please add a regression alert rule: if throughput for top-10 models drops >8% vs weekly baseline, send pager to eng-runtime.

jamal: I'll draft the rule and add a perf-check to CI that runs the microbench variants. we should also record head/count kv_dim metadata in model profiles so selector can make decisions without heuristics.

maria: :thumbsup: add unit tests to validate no-change for GQA models that are already aligned (e.g., Qwen configured with num_key_value_heads that divides 64).

alex: great. follow-ups: - PR up by EOD - perf CI run scheduled - alert + model-profile metadata ticket.

ops-bot: ci: perf-check triggered; results pending (will post thread update).

sara: nice work team, this aligns with the Optimize recommendations for cache-friendly layouts. small changes, big wins.

alex: agree. posting links to flamegraphs & perf diffs in the PR thread.

ops-bot: perf-check: baseline vs canary diff: throughput +10.9%, p99 -18.7%, memory +6.9%.
